comment: Crowded
Some steep inclines, but very enjoyable conditions. Lovely views of the falls and pond on Meadow Trail. Horse flies were out for blood
No flush toilet. The falls was far from the viewpoint
Trail is well maintained overall, slightly over grown in some parts. Buggy in the second half of the hike.
very pretty trail! plenty of parking available and a gorgeous waterfall. some parts are a little overgrown so watch out for ticks. lots of bugs on the trail. pass required!
Fire trail, sick views with cool waterfall
Some parts of the trail are steep especially leading up to the waterfall if you’re not very fit or don’t hike regularly you might find it a bit challenging.
No restrooms on the trail. Only in the parking lot.
Fantastic trail
There are up and down hills, and trail right next to the cliff. Need proper hiking shoes to finish the whole loop. Be aware of the ticks, I saw one on my dog.

Great scenery all around and free of anything for kilometres, allowing you to get immersed in nature and the beautiful forests and calm waters. The falls are nice at the end, and the trails are easy to follow. A little overcrowded during peak times but overall really nice park and trails.
Can’t get close to the fall but the trails are pretty.

Awesome trail. Leads to a beautiful waterfall. Definitely didn’t climb behind the no trespassing fence to get a better view  few uphill spots along the trail were kinda tough but all around fun trail.
Good hike
Nice trail to see some colour change. The trail was in good condition. Unfortunately, the viewing platform for the falls was fenced off, so the view wasn’t great. This was an easy hike overall.
Not much for views, but the trail itself is beautiful. Close to Toronto!
Easy open trails and more difficult ones available if one prefers to get their heart rate up.

Great variety of scenery, lake, meadows, forest, waterfall. Well marked and easy to navigate. Some hills but adds to the experience. Need to purchase a permit before hand if driving in, otherwise free if you dropped off outside. Great trail
Good hike, lots of ups and downs. Peaceful and beautiful views!
Nice trial
Definitely not kid friendly. I went by myself and it was not bad! Definitely a workout but the views are worth it
It’s a lot of up and down and the trails aren’t all fixed up, not good for a wagon or stroller, the views and accomplishments of finishing this trail is totally worth it all!
Great hiking location with good hills to climb, not to busy but parking lot needs to be repaired lots of pot holes
Easy and well groomed.  Views are plain.
Lovely
Permit required to enter park. Trail was well maintained and clearly marked.
Lovely trail, dog friendly, nice spots to take breaks. Just a bit confusing to navigate if you don’t have this app as there are many short cuts and side trails.
Went on a wet and rainy day, which meant very few people in the trail. Was nice to have the trail to ourselves with the dogs.
Not kid or elderly friendly. Mostly uphills, and sharp inclines. Maybe another time but not this time...
great trail!! good conditions
Nice trail
Awesome trail with minimal people lots of water snacks good hiking boots are a must If you take the bruce trail lots of climbing down.Make sure that you use the rope going down the hill
Great trail! Prepare for quite a bit of uphill! Personally i think you can skip the side trail to Cataract Falls as the view is not anything crazy. Overall great place to get your sweat on!
Elevation gains and dips are fun. Not crowded and good scenery.
Great, easy trail
Lovely for leg day workout. Go the long way to reap the waterfall reward .

Great park in Caledon. You can walk in the meadows along a small lake or through the woods or take a trip along the roaring river. Lots to explore and do. Beautiful lookout to the falls. My pup and I loved exploring with hidden places to swim and fish. Great spot!
The whole on-line registration process is a b***h and is better done at home.

Good quality trail with some up and downhill sections. Forested portions as well as open meadows. Falls view is OK, but partially obstructed. Pretty quiet on a weekday summer morning. Only saw other people on the way out, about 6 of them in total. From the falls view, took one of the steep side trails to get to Meadow Trail to shortcut the way back to parking lot. Total 4.9 miles (7.8km), 520' gain (158m). 2:25 total time, with a few short breaks.
Forks of the Credit
A little buggy, might want to bring bug spray. Great trail; views are excellent.
Very nice  trail I loved it
A lot of mosquitos. But I like the challenging  trails

Went at 8 am. Done by 10. Started to get busy by 10am. Part of the trail is shaded in trees. The start and end are in fields so direct sun. There are some access points to water (for dogs). Trail is narrow in areas.
Good scenery and a cool waterfall. Came here in August and there were lots of mosquitoes so bring insect repellent. Need a permit to get into the parking lot.

Weather was cool today.. perfect for a hike. The trail was good. Very peaceful. Only ran into 2 other people there. Some steep parts.. as is mentioned in here it’s a good idea to take the trail to your right to start. I like that if you feel like you need to cut the trail shorter you can.

Great trail! Met a friendly snapping turtle that is clearly used to being fed. Lots of wildlife and of course, the waterfall. 

Wasn’t too busy on a Saturday evening.
Mosquitoes and bees and weeds
Nice trail but not a good spot for photography . The water fall is too hard to get to

Don’t forget to reserve your day pass parking before you go.  
Great place, starting to get very crowded. Everyone under estimates the distance to the Falls. So you get asked every few corners if this is the right way.  Other than that, this is my favourite place to hike.   First time bringing my 4year old and 1.5 year old.   They both did a lot of the walking.
Bug spray is needed and there’s lots of long grass/plants.
So far the best! Easy to intermediate level.
Moderately difficult at certain parts of the trails with beautiful views. A lot of mosquitoes so dress appropriately
Beautiful trail. Tons of mosquitoes - definitely dress appropriately. Need a day pass parking permit from Ontario parks to enter the automated gate.
Nice loop hike with sun and shade. Viewing platform for the waterfall not accessible so one part of this was “out and back”. Doing the falls at the second half was a good “reward”.
The trails was serene and peaceful with lots greenery and lookout points for the waterfall and lake. My dog loved it!!

Part of this loop is closed for construction. It looks like some people  went through anyway, and we were able to go around and piece it together. As others have said, the beginning and end of the hike are less interesting—pretty flat and windswept. Otherwise, as described!
Nice down by the water, but the badlands were windy today.

Nice sections, some good verticals but Parking is a challenge.  A day pass at the Prov park seemed the best option.  Lots of road sections but they too are pretty here.  Not muddy (March 31) and the valley portions are quite diverse.

If you have a dog, MAKE SURE to check them for ticks; we found 4 on our white dog when we were done. 
Really good trail, conditions solid (not very muddy). We were able to do most of it by going up the stairs at the river, doubling back then crossing back down bruce so don’t be discouraged by the partial closure of Dominion at the falls!

The parking AllTrails suggests you use is covered with no parking signs - same with other nearby off roads. It appears the only way in now is through the main gates. A bunch of the trails and highlights are unfortunately closed for renovation (like the good view of the falls), but you can still sneak in and see a bit if you feel up to it. We couldn't do the full loop suggested here. The trails were dry and very walkable when I went on March 13. Very anticlimactic and flat for the portion in/out to the parking. The falls were beautiful, but in future would pick going elsewhere until the repairs are done.
Trail was excellent. good for the cardio
Was icy today so the trail was a bit dangerous but a lot of it should be melted by mow
Icy.  Need your crampons.  Lots of up and down hills.  Great views.  Waterfall

The thick snowfall on caledon created a really cool layer of ice on the whole park.

This park is my favourite ontario park hands down.

Snow is well packed going to and from the waterfall and Bruce Trail, but not as well on the trans Canada sections. This park is always pretty and a decent challenge. Frozen waterfall is always gorgeous but from any of the official viewpoints you can barely see it. There are risks for better views but for seasoned (and prepared!) hikers with the necessary safety gear it's worth it.

Caledon falls stays in my rotation of top Ontario parks. Heads up - trails are not snow maintained, and the path between meadow trail & dominion trail doesn’t exist (we walked through the trees lol)

Make sure to see the falls!!
Really nice cold weather trail hike. Part of the loop by the waterfall is currently closed for the winter, creating an out and back with elevation to see the waterfall.
Very muddy in the meadow area.
kind of slippery in some parts and quite and incline for most parts. good work out
Great trail, mostly flat but with some inclines. Fall foliage and Cataract falls along the trail.

Nice.

 Falls look out closed for erosion.
so many mosquitos
Lots of mosquitos in a couple sections but had some nice views. Waterfall lookout is closed off right now.
The trail was blocked by falls.
Bring proper hiking shoes, bugs are moderate
This trail is not for biking.

Lots of hills and climbing but very doable. Nice and shady for the most part. Trail is closed at the waterfall and forces you back out and around. Still can make it a loop. But waterfall is a dead end with lots of hills to climb

Bruce Meadow Dominion Loop is an absolute gem of a hike trail! The trail is well-maintained, making it a joy to navigate through its winding path with chirping birds accompanying you along the way. The peaceful ambiance and stunning natural beauty make Bruce Meadow Dominion Loop a must-visit for nature lovers and hikers alike.

It gets steep at some parts, adding an invigorating challenge to the hike and making it a fantastic workout.
Beautiful hike, nice waterfall. The route was closed off near the waterfall.  Went a direction with a lot of hill climbing. Good work out.

Very quite area w little to no other people on the trials, nice for afternoon strolls. 
Only downside is there isn’t any parking near by and is placed in a tricky spot to get to in comparison to majority of other provincial parks.
A few flies but overall a great hike!!

Always a pretty hike. We were surprised by how much ice is still on the trail so be ready for that. The waterfall section is closed off. The view from from forks of credit road is really nice. Lots of mud.
Lots of ice going towards the waterfall  and mud on the way back on the Trans Canada Trail
Trail is icy and can be hidden under a powdery layer of snow
Beginning is vey muddy.
Great trail through forests and meadows. Very icy and slippery today.

As has been pointed out the trail from the parking lot is alternately muddy and icy. GORE-TEX uppers and crampons will be your best friend. The canopied portions on the Bruce Trail is soft snow and quite beautiful. Navigating around the falls is discouraged but if you have to (as we did) take extra precautions.
Loved this trail. Very nice after the snow.

Very muddy in places (sticky, slippery mud), not well built so washed out in a lot of places too. Couldn’t get a good view of the falls from anywhere on the trail. I did see there was a viewing platform that had been dismantled and they plan to rebuild so maybe once that’s done you’ll be able to see the falls from that. Trail overall was just okay.

Dominion to meadow trail was closed, and you might want to get a parking permit ahead of time but it seems like they also have a few spots available on a first come first served basis. Overall, great trail, not very well marked when switching to the Trans Canada trail, but the all trails guide helped.

LOOP CLOSED. This is an OK hike. It is definitely easy, not moderate, so if you are looking for a workout - choose another trail. The waterfall comes out of a concrete tunnel so not as pretty as I had expected.￼
Easy hike in cool weather. I come to climb the hills.
very nice to go on trail, hike, bike etc….during Fall
Beautiful fall trail. No mud.

This was a moderately challenging hike with lots of inclines and declines. My fitbit reported 91 "floors" during this hike. We did the falls lookout trail and it was super disappointing!! You cannot even see the falls from the lookout because it's blocked by trees and very far away! Would not recommend. The trails are beautiful during fall but otherwise I don't think I would complete this hike again!
Access to the fall on the west is temporarily closed
Beautiful but a bit disappointing that the trail wasn’t rerouted close to where the lookout used to be
A part of it is off-road, can’t get thru. Need to reroute.
Nice easy
Did this hike mid-September and it was pretty dope and easy. Not crowded and no bugs. Highly recommend!
Perfect hike. Great inclines and lovely waterfall!

Waterfall path is unfortunately closed. Otherwise, a pretty decent trail consisting of some forests and meadows. Went early in the morning, around 8:30 am, to avoid a big rush and there wasn't too many people. More people started showing up at around 11:30am.

Views are not that good of the river and falls, very disappointed because I thought it would be a great view. Lots of ups and down and rocky terrain so a good challenge if that’s what you’re looking for.

Beautiful views but access to the waterfall is limited, a couple hundred meters is as close as you can get from the south (July 2022) and access is one way.  The Ruins Trail from the north does not connect to the southerly route (also one way), so there is no loop at this point.
Waterfall closed, get yourself a mosquito spray and cover your neck .. good hike otherwise
Lots of inclines but beautiful
To many mosquitos
Beautiful trail! The water was amazing. Definitely going back this summer!
Lovely trail with some good variety of terrain but kms 3-6 were closed for maintenance and we had to detour. I suggest checking the park notices before going
nice and dry out there today!!!
A lot of fun! Good view of a waterfall and a pond/river. Walking in both a field and woodland with a few ups and downs to take your breath away! Would do again!
Packed snow all along - very nice walking conditions (kids im T-shirt!)
Great trail! Lots of fun. Route closed near the waterfalls.
Part of the trail by the waterfall is closed, which is fine. Follow the signs to the waterfall, then go back and do the rest of the trail. It’s a great winter hike.
great!

We really enjoyed this walk. We took the path starting to the left when it splits after the parking lot. Some inclines to get the heart rate up, a detour to sit by the water, and an at-a-distance view of the falls. We really felt like we got away from the city. Note that the AllTrails map is not accurate at the moment—you can walk to a point where you can see the falls, but you cannot continue through and must retrace your path before heading back to the parking lot.
It was my first time on this trail, and first for this park, for that matter. It was recommended by friends who have walked the trails here at Forks for many years. I loved it.
Amazing trail! Parts of the trails were closed near the water falls. 10/10 would recommend this trail
Great trail but the waterfall is not worth the hike
Incredibly beautiful part of the BT, maybe my favourite yet…lots of climbing/elevation! Have to pay a 7.50$ provincial park fee if entering thru the park-very worth it.
Beautiful Trail!

Beautiful trail with clear paths! When arriving at the first fork, I suggest veering left (Trans-Canada trail) for a scenic descent and overall easier time. The loop around the falls lookout is currently closed, so you can only view from a far distance then come back the same way.

Most memorable was that the trail took us through many different scanties, from tree-covered “tunnels” to open fields. The fall colour would’ve been so much prettier and the trail condition nicer if it hadn’t rained the whole week before. Overall a great experience!
Perfect day trail in great shape. Followed the river for a bit rough trail but walkable.
Great hike!

Note: the trail shown here goes off marked trails and down the escarpment. Not for anyone with mobility issues. At the bottom end of the trail, I continued along the Bruce and climbed the far side of the escarpment.
Good trails, no bugs. Well marked. Only downside is you cannot get close to the falls.
Nice hike, too bad you can't get close to the falls. It took us about 2.5hrs to hike 7kms. Went on Monday and it wasn't very busy.

Trail was just OKAY in my opinion. It gets very steep along the Bruce trail (which is amazing if you're looking for a workout). The falls were lackluster, and the views were subpar; on a more positive note I saw a lot of interesting bird species (if you're into that kind of thing). Also, this trail is not a loop, its out -and-back, which was a surprise. Overall, it gave me the workout I was looking for but I don't think I will be returning.
trail to see view to the falls is closed

Great trails with very little bugs!
It was my daughter’s and I first time on this trail and we weren’t disappointed…
Easy breezy.
awesome hike,

Beautiful trails in this park. We did Meadow trail. It was about 6 to 7 kms long. Writing review of meadow trail here because I don't see meadow trail post anywhere here. You have to reserve parking before going here. We booked for 2 slots since we were going to go for longer trail. There are ups and downs .. good butt exercise :)
We do see waterfall at the end, was beautiful. The pathway towards the falls was closed at this time, not sure why. Some parts of the trail is shady and some parts were sunny. There were signs along the trails, so was easy to figure out our way. Was a great hike on a hot summer day and was not too busy. Everyone were mindful of keeping distance. We will be coming back!
BANGER
Great trail. We went with our 8 year old and it was fine. Havent done the entire loop because we went to check out the falls.

Well maintained trail, it has washrooms , unfortunately the access to the falls is closed. As you get closer to the falls the walk gets challenging. $7.50 for parking, now you can book online on Ontario Parks website

awesome hiking trails.
falls are restricted & view isn't great.
Enjoyed hiking this trial, nice views , best to be there early on weekends as it get busy
Wonderful!
Gorgeous hike with challenging hills
It’s a bit difficult trail but it is fun. Lots of ups and downs. Loved it esp. my daughter.

Went during the week so it wasn’t too busy. Crossed by maybe 2-3 people on our 8k. Different types of terrain and every turn had new scenery. Was extremely beautiful and well maintained. Signage also made it easy.
Weather was amazing so the trail was very busy but not too bad, still a lovely hike. Bring sunscreen!
The loop is closed off from once you view the falls, and so you have to go back the way you came for that section. The falls are stunning but vantage point isn’t that impressive.
leave no trace, don't pass trash.
Waterfall was a tad underwhelming as the trail right to it was blocked off. $6.50 for 4hrs parking
Great trail!
Beautiful day to be outside, trail was not busy but a bit muddy
Good trail, some big ups and beautiful scenery.
Trails were great, muddy in some parts but a good pair of boots will get your through it! Some ice still on the back paths but nothing crazy
Super muddy in some sections, icy in others. Proper boots are a must! Beautiful beautiful day out
Trail to the waterfalls was very icy. Spikes are a must at this time.
glad I own crampons
its our first time here. its a nice trail. will be coming back for sure. Our dog loves it so much - no steel staircase and lots of water.

The path is practically all icy... must wear the crampons for grip. 
If well prepared, the path is well marked and tracked, and the forest is beautiful!

We took the Meadow trail and then the lower trail to the falls and back. It was about 7 km in and out but felt longer with the descent into the valley and then the climb out the other side to see the falls. The trail past the falls was closed so we had to go back the way we came. Popular trail but didn’t feel crowded. Trail was covered by snow with relatively good traction. Varied scenery from meadow, lake, forest and falls. Washroom available.

We parked in the McLaren road lot and walked a short loop. Kettle lake was frozen over but still pretty in the snow. This is an easy walk and not long. There are no heavily wooded areas and the trail is always wide enough for two. If you are looking for wilderness this is not the place. The west side of this trail is a lot more spectacular with the falls but we had a beautiful day and a nice walk. It's a bit busier than the trail we are used to further north but try to go on a weekday!
Once we were on the Bruce trail it was great but there is no parking at the south trail head. Lots of no parking signs.
Very  icy so do wear proper boots with spikes. I enjoyed it.

This trail is so well marked including the side trails. Icy in some areas and steep so ice cleats would be suggested. Trail does not continue past the falls anymore so you have to turn around and go back the same way. Great hike.
Very icey!
way too icy on the trails. someone was even skating on them!
Beautiful trail, it’s a shame that the trail is closed after the waterfall though. If you are hiking after a snowfall, spikes or snowshoes would be highly recommended.
Beautiful, specially with all the snow.  definitely need hiking boots in winter.
Some icy sections in the meadow otherwise an nice loop. Moderately travelled.
Beautiful trail. Pretty busy though. Can’t really see to much of the falls right now because the trail kinda stops because of erosion. Some pretty steep parts
Pay parking lots of options for loops
such a beautiful trail this time of the year
Very nice trail through forests and meadows
Steep in sections, beautiful with the leaves fallen
Not much to see this time of the year.

beautiful in the fall. the trail was cut off at the falls and had signage indicating you had to go back the way you came in, however a quick offroading side trail got me back onto the loop. I went on a monday, the trail was a touch busy, but not crowded by any means. overall lovely hike, would go again!
Awesome
Get here at opening to avoid the crowd which started to build around 11:00 on a Sunday. You can see the falls but the trail leading through / past the falls was closed on our hike day (20 Sep 20).

This was a great trail but busy as it was a Saturday and part of the loop is missing. The section near the falls is damaged so I hoofed  it up the hill to catch the loop and continue on. I would recommend this for sure but during the week!
Gorgeous hike. Well maintained and has different options depending on how much distance you want to cover. Had a fantastic time with my friends.
Can’t get close to the falls :(
Great trail- some areas were blocked off

I arrived at 9:45 on a Saturday morning and the lot was about 1/3 full. By the time I returned to the parking area at 12 it was definitely busier but not a total nightmare, still a few spots left. This trail loop is a really good 2 hour workout. A few steep but brief climbs to work up a sweat. There were people of all ages and abilities out on the trail. Definitely not good for strollers. There are lots of options for different routes and the trails are sufficiently marked. Cell signal was non-existent in some areas so be sure to download or print off a map. As per other reviews part of the trail was closed at the north end of the loop but there are other routes available so no biggie. I had no issues with bugs.
Beautiful Trail. Definitely need the Hoka Speed Goat 4 shoes.

Very nice trail. We left the lot at about 8:30 on a friday morning and saw almost nobody until we were back to the parking lot, so based on other comments, much less travelled during the week. Bugs are gone, get out and enjoy!
Lots of trash being thrown beside the trail.  Saw a woman toss a diaper out on the trail. Too many people.

Great for a beginner! Took a 27 pound pack walked the trail. Perfect great practice in difference terrain. Nice views. Pretty clean but please don’t add any trash!!! Beautiful park Thankyou Caledon and parks!

This trail is poorly marked on AllTrails, the area they suggest you park at is closed and parking barred. Go to the main Forks of the Credit entrance; you have to pay to park. Waterfall viewing platform is closed and associated section of the Bruce Trail is closed. This trail is very busy and you can only complete about 7 km; parts that are open are lovely but there was lots of garbage and it was packed by the time we left at 11 am. Do not recommend.

Good to enjoy with kids.

Water and land frogs are off trails
Beautiful views and a trail that has everything for everyone. You will come across fascinating views, experience flats, elevations and demotions throughout. Highly recommended.

A beautiful trail for a good hike. Lots of open vistas. Start the trail early to avoid the crowd. We started around 7.30 and was able to complete the loop in 3 hours and by 10.30 the parking lot was already full. The fall view is not much impressive but the walk to the viewpoint is a good cardio. Would recommend spending time by the lake to take in the morning calmness of the waters. Take precautions for mosquitoes especially in the Dominion trail portion of the loop.
Easy going to start and then really hit some pretty good elevation gains whilst following the Bruce Trail sections!
Go early. We did the trail starting at 8.30 and it was lovely. Lots of crowds near the parking lot as we ended our hike at noon.

Really disappointing.  This was the busiest hiking trial I’ve ever been on! We left shortly after exploring the trailhead and encountering crowds. Cars were lining up to park and traffic was jammed all the way up the access road. Given the high volume of hikers it was impossible to socially distance on the trail. Just too many people!

Go early to the trail, by noon its VERY BUSY (went on a Saturday)
Did the full loop and some side trails. Easy to moderate terrain. Once you get deeper into trail not many people. some good uphills and shady areas. Overall good trail for the distance. 
Doggy friendly too.
I saw a snake (harmless one I’m sure) but screamed quite loudly anyway

Arrived just after park opened - good parking. Loved the whole journey. Too bad trail closed at the falls (signs posted stating that fact, so no surprise) and the climb up ended with disappointing views of the falls, but still enjoyable.  Noticed litter on trail by the falls (shame on those people) but rest of the hike was good!  I found signs posted to be helpful and rubber hoses used as hand-rails by steep hills/stairs is brilliant!  A few steep climbs, but nothing that wasn’t manageable.  Lots of birds singing but didn’t see any other wildlife. Lilac field was beautiful. 
Will go again and walk some other trails. 
I recommend this!
serene!!!

Took our 2yr old out to try it. Lots of ups and downs but he handled it like a champ. He walked a good 1km of our 4KM hike. We brought our child carrier back back though so came prepared. Saw people with strollers and wagons... I don’t recommend it. Not the trail for those.

Did this trail in the summer. As mentioned, google the parking lot access to this, don’t use what all trails says.
Nice run, one of my first trail runs. Easy, flat. Easily enough marked trail. Parts of the trail was closed but people were hopping over the barriers to see the falls.  I’m planning on running it again this winter.
Lovely fall day for a hike. We cut the trail a bit short at 6k which is easy to do with all the crossing paths. Great elevation changes and vistas.

Found this trail a tad bit disappointing after all the effort to make it to view the waterfall only for it to be closed off. The best part was only a small stretch of the river. The hike back to parking felt more like a punishment, but that’s probably because of feeling salty after not being able to relax and unwind at the waterfall.
very good route!!

Nice trail in the winter - quite icy near the parking area but got much better as we continued. Look up the parking area separately (the location provided in the directions tab in the AllTrails app does not provide parking). Great spot.

Hiking this trail for 25 years. Loveliest in the fall but also heavily trafficked at that time. Shame about the break in the trail at the fall viewing area as the outer loop was great but you “can” be a scofflaw and jump the fence (a little treacherous in winter and tricky with two large dogs) or see the falls (south-west approach, generally clockwise loop) and then return, re-climb the hill, and hike the upper trail back (sticking to the left) and down the stairs.  Official parking (north east corner) is $5.25 for 2 hrs. Or you can hike in along th Cataract trail from Mississauga Rd. I’ve never tried parking at Dominion rd (residential private dead end).
had a wonderful winter walk!!

Loved this trail! I can’t wait to go back in the spring. We didn’t get to go all the way to the falls because the lookout was closed but it was so icy it was almost impossible to get there. It will be a great hike when the snow melts!
absolutly love this trail. one of my favorite in the area! so much to explore off the trail. all though you have to cross restricted areas. but if your risk taker its worth it.

Parking situation on a nice sunny weekend was awful.  Official parking lots full and side streets were blocked off.  Ended up starting way off trail.  Once on trail, crowded.  It's a nice trail but only recommend it as a week day excursion.

The trails were lovely and well kept but the parking situation was terrible. When we arrived we had to park in the overflow lot, no problem, however, once we returned from our hike we were blocked in!  We managed to squeeze out of our spot only to become frustrated by traffic entering the park.  Cars were parked on both sides of the street only allowing for traffic to flow in one direction. Overall a disappointing end to an otherwise lovely day.

It was great time to enjoy fall leaves. The lake was quiet and peaceful. It was light rainy and the little foggy weather made the scenery fantastic. Loved it. However, the fall was less impressive (disappointing).

Perfect trail for early fall.. some parts in shade and lots of sunshine area.At least two nice spots to rest at the river bank. Highly recommended trail !!!
PS. it is good to park on Fork on the Credit Rd,before Dominion rd,  along the road, but watch for the signs, police is patrolling during a weekend .
Great view of waterfalls

I would mark this trail as easy. Trail head is easily accessible with a big paid-parking lot. 1st half of the trail is fairly busy, rolling meadows, with lots of weekend-warriors. Once you get past the beginning half the crowds die down a bit and it's easy wooded trails with shady cover. Lots of opportunity to extend the hike with side trails. Keep an eye on where you're going as you may not notice and end up on a side-trail.

Small beach at the end, probably wouldn't swim in there..
Some beautiful trails and a nice waterfall to stop at for lunch, or spend the day by the lake.

The Dominion Trail leading to the falls was a nice hike. The falls are blocked off now, sadly. Trails need better markers for North, south, etc. I trekked almost the entire area as the north west side of the Bruce trail was also closed off. Enjoyed my day despite the rain!
Has some intense hills in certain areas. beautiful small park the waterfall is amazing and can be seen in two areas. some of the trail is washed out due to rain and erosion over time.

it's a lovely trail. lots of intersecting trails so it's important to pay attention to where you are going. there's a lot of flat ground but the hike to the falls is steep and quite the workout. it gets slippery in wet weather. The falls are closed off and the trail doesn't loop around so it's a one way walk to the falls and back. it's beautiful and scenic with access to the river at various points. it's one of my favourite places to hike.

A great trail system, vert enjoyable.
Bruce Trail certainly an easy trail, Dominion has several steep inclines, water poles and steps. 20 seconds after reading the ‘no mountain biking’ sign, a guy went by on one. Very easy loop system to contend with, relatively quiet, with some out enjoying a hike, and then the odd walker going by in their Levi’s and fashion trainers. The coordinates when you click ‘Directions’ on this app takes you to the entrance on Dominion Street, which requires you to park on the main street and then walk across the bridge and onto Dominion, to the beginning of the trail.

Interesting trail and an enjoyable hike.  

Some things worth noting:

The main user access point is via the access road at the NE corner.  There's absolutely no parking at the indicated point on the map.

There's a fair amount of poison ivy along the trail margins.  Make sure you can recognize it before setting out.

There's a break in the trail at the NW corner, at the falls.  It looks like the trail got washed out.  There are fences to stop people going past this point although the fences are easily negotiated and the trail's really not too bad if you're careful.
